question: Which inputs does the originated line actually use?

missing_information: Every advanced input (pace, efficiency, injuries, personnel) is missing; only final scores are used.

question: How accurate is the originated line out of sample?
known_facts_verified: Mean absolute error 9.16 points vs 10.89 for the naive reference line across 89 out-of-sample games (weeks 4-10); improvement +1.74 points, 95% bootstrap CI [0.76, 2.74], permutation p<0.05 after BH correction.
missing_information: Only 89 games from one season; no market benchmark; the confidence interval is wide.
how_to_discover_official_first: Extend the results set to earlier seasons from the official by-week schedule pages, then re-run scripts/model.py.

question: Can the model beat a sportsbook closing line?

question: Does recency weighting add skill?
known_facts_verified: Three-week half-life weighting scored +1.59 points vs +1.74 for uniform weighting; the confidence intervals overlap and week-to-week margin persistence is r=0.087 (n = 228 team-game pairs, published as descriptive with no interval or p-value after the F55 correction).
missing_information: 89 games; the variants are highly correlated, so differences are poorly resolved.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-test on several seasons with a pre-registered comparison on a held-out period.

question: Do game totals carry signal?

how_to_discover_official_first: Add two or three official team-stat inputs with cross-validated shrinkage and re-test (Suggestion S12).

question: How are same-game parlay legs correlated?

how_to_discover_official_first: Pre-register leg definitions and grade them over several seasons before pricing any ticket.

question: Do our own margin projections beat predicting nothing, out of sample?
status: Answered — yes for three rules, but not decisively
known_facts_verified: Eight competing rules were evaluated on 96 unseen games. Three (S5, S6, S7) beat the zero baseline with a 95% interval entirely above zero; the strongest of those is S6 at 7.1% error reduction, interval [0.4%, 13.8%], winner accuracy 67.0%, Brier 0.2284 against a 0.25 coin-flip baseline. The highest raw score, S4 at 7.7%, has an interval crossing zero.
missing_information: More weeks, and a pre-registered rule set so new rules are not chosen after seeing scores. No rule currently survives the multiple-comparison adjustment.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-run scripts/model.py as official weeks are added.

question: Does simply backing the home team every week work?
status: Answered — no, it is worse than doing nothing
known_facts_verified: The home-field-only rule scored -1.0% skill (negative), with 40.4% winner accuracy and a Brier of 0.2539, worse than the 0.25 coin-flip baseline.
missing_information: Nothing further; the answer is stable enough to act on for this sample.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-test each season; home advantage has changed over time.

question: Can this project originate a useful game total?
known_facts_verified: Not measurably. The best total projection missed by 10.99 points per game against 11.04 for simply projecting the league average every game, a gap of 0.05 points, and its correlation with the actual total (r = 0.064) is not distinguishable from zero.
missing_information: A larger sample and better features (pace, weather, venue, officiating tendencies) would be needed before trusting a total.
how_to_discover_official_first: Re-run scripts/model.py as official weeks are added.

question: Do the two teams' scores in the same game depend on each other?
status: Answered — no measurable dependence on this sample
known_facts_verified: r = 0.076 over 137 games, 95% interval [-0.093, 0.241]. The interval crosses zero.
missing_information: A larger sample, and player-level or drive-level data to explain any dependence that exists.
how_to_discover_official_first: Recompute from the official ledger as weeks are added.

question: Is week-to-week scoring momentum real?
known_facts_verified: Team points scored in consecutive games correlate at r = 0.068 over 228 consecutive team pairs; points allowed correlate at r = 0.063. Both intervals cross zero.
missing_information: Nothing further; treat momentum claims as unsupported until they are measured.
how_to_discover_official_first: Recompute from the official ledger as weeks are added.

question: Do two different model families diversify each other?
known_facts_verified: The margin prediction errors of two structurally different models are correlated at r = 0.981 over 96 games. Stacking similar models repeats the same mistake rather than diversifying it.
missing_information: Genuinely different inputs (availability, play-level data) would be needed for real diversification.
how_to_discover_official_first: Recompute with scripts/model.py.

question: Is the model more accurate when it is more confident?
known_facts_verified: The selectivity table splits results by projection size. Accuracy inside the largest-projection bands is not consistently better than inside the smallest bands, and the bands hold few games.
missing_information: More games per band, which needs more weeks of results.
how_to_discover_official_first: Recompute with scripts/model.py.

question: Within one game, do the side leg and the total leg move together?

question: Which log is the pre-registered backtest corpus: 136, 137 or 150 games?
status: Open - decision required before any metric is re-published
known_facts_verified: 136 = weeks 1-9 as held in the feed (16+16+16+16+15+14+14+14+15). 137 = that log plus the Thursday Nov 12 game. 150 = everything the official standings now show as completed through Week 10 (149+149+2 team-games). The Week 10 slate itself is 14 games, listed in data/games_week10_2026.csv with 13 blank results.
missing_information: Whether the owner wants published metrics recomputed on a longer corpus (which changes every error, interval and gate number on the site) or frozen at 137 with the gap disclosed.
how_to_discover_official_first: Nothing further to read: the 13 scores are transcribed and reconciled (data/games_week10_backfill_2026.csv). This is a choice about versioning, recorded as proposal P09 on the Review console.

question: Is a dated capture of an official Week-n report reproducible, or does the page move underneath it?
